chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The testimony of the son of adultery is not valid.

key_terms.وَلَدِ الزِّنَى: Son of adultery / Child of illicit relations

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child of adultery valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi establishes that the testimony of a 'walad al-zina' (child of fornication) is rejected, reflecting the principle that illicit sexual relations carry specific legal consequences beyond mere sin. Scholars note that this ruling underscores the importance of lineage purity and the distinct legal status assigned to children born from zina, distinguishing them from those with established legitimate lineage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The testimony of the son of adultery is not allowed’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The testimony of one born out of wedlock is not admissible.’”
